title: Liftoff from the launch pad
place: A coastal launch pad at dawn, a tall white rocket on a steel tower, umbilical arms swinging away, a wall of flame and steam boiling out
situation: Engines ignite, the clamps release, and the rocket rises slowly while every camera, bird and spectator for miles watches
cast: three astronauts strapped on their backs
pad leader in a hard hat
visualTropes: ice chunks falling off the tank
a flame tail brighter than the sun
jokeHooks: the rocket clears the tower the way a build clears its slowest step: very slowly at first
one umbilical stays attached a second too long, like a lingering lock
the pelicans arrive for every launch like bots on every PR

title: Crowds on the beach for launch
place: A packed beach and causeway miles from the pad, families on car roofs, cameras on tripods, coolers, flags and a giant countdown clock
situation: Thousands of spectators wait through hold after hold, counting down together each time the clock restarts
cast: kid in a cardboard space helmet
visualTropes: a distant rocket like a pencil
jokeHooks: the countdown holds at T-minus 10 like a deploy waiting on one last check
the crowd counts down together three times for a single launch
the retired engineer explains the bug to strangers before the report is out

title: Firing room countdown
place: A long tiered room of glowing consoles, everyone in white shirts and skinny ties, ashtrays and coffee, a big window toward the distant pad
situation: The launch director polls each station for go or no-go, and one controller hesitates on a strange reading
visualTropes: a go/no-go poll around the room
jokeHooks: one station says no-go and the whole release halts, like one red required check
the go/no-go poll is a code review with fifty approvers
the strange reading is a flaky sensor that has cried wolf before

title: Landing on the Moon with seconds left
place: A spindly gold-foil lunar lander descending over a gray cratered plain, dust blowing outward, the black sky and the blue Earth above
situation: Alarms blare as the computer overloads; the commander takes manual control and hunts for a flat spot with fuel running out
jokeHooks: the computer throws an alarm code nobody has seen outside a simulation
landing with seconds of fuel left, like merging minutes before the freeze
the landing site in the plan turns out to be full of boulders, like the spec versus reality

title: First steps and a stubborn flag
place: The gray lunar surface beside a gold-foil lander, footprints in fine dust, a long black shadow, Earth hanging in the black sky
situation: Astronauts bounce around planting a flag that will not stay up, collecting rocks and reading a checklist on their cuffs
cast: pilot with a camera on the chest
visualTropes: a flag with a crooked rod
jokeHooks: the flag's extension rod jams like a half-applied migration
the checklist on the cuff is a runbook with a step nobody tested in low gravity
the TV camera broadcasts upside down, like a log in the wrong timezone

title: Lunar rover across the highlands
place: Rolling lunar highlands, a little open-frame electric rover bouncing over craters, rooster tails of dust, mountains on the horizon
situation: Two astronauts race the rover to a far crater, bouncing off the seats, with a fender held on by maps and tape
visualTropes: a dish antenna on the rover
jokeHooks: the taped fender is a quick fix that ships to the Moon
the rover's top speed is an SLA everyone brags about
the navigation map is cached from orbit, months out of date

title: Spacewalk to fix a broken panel
place: Open orbit high above a swirling blue Earth, an astronaut tethered to a space station truss, a jammed solar wing, tools floating
situation: An astronaut must free a jammed solar panel with improvised tools while the station races toward the night side
visualTropes: Earth's curve and a sunrise line
a wrench floating out of reach
jokeHooks: the fix is a hand-made tool built from a toothbrush, like a script nobody should ship
the lost wrench becomes permanent debris, like a dangling feature flag
the repair window is ninety minutes, the length of a full CI run

title: Docking in orbit
place: Two spacecraft closing in over the blue Earth, thrusters puffing, a probe aimed at a docking cone, sunlight glinting off foil
situation: The pilot nudges the capsule toward the station while the docking target drifts and everyone holds their breath
cast: station crew watching through a window
jokeHooks: two systems dock only when both versions agree on the latch protocol
the docking takes eleven tiny corrections, like iterating on review feedback
contact and capture are two separate checks, like merged and deployed

title: Fiery reentry
place: A cone-shaped capsule plunging heat-shield first through the upper atmosphere, a trail of plasma and glowing debris, stars giving way to blue
situation: Radio goes dark during the blackout and everyone waits to hear if the heat shield held
visualTropes: a plasma glow around the capsule
jokeHooks: the radio blackout is a deploy with no logs for four minutes
the heat shield ablates on purpose, like a cache built to be thrown away
the first word after blackout lands like a green check after a long build

title: Splashdown and recovery
place: A wide blue Pacific under a bright sky, a capsule bobbing under three orange-and-white parachutes, helicopters and frogmen around it
situation: The capsule splashes down, flips upside down, and frogmen leap from a helicopter to attach a flotation collar before it sinks
visualTropes: a helicopter downdraft rippling the sea
jokeHooks: the capsule lands upside down and must be righted, like a rollback after release
the parachute count drops from three to two and everyone holds their breath
the seagull lands first and claims the ship, like the first bot comment

title: Welcome on the recovery ship
place: The deck of an aircraft carrier crowded with sailors in whites, a brass band, a sign WELCOME HOME, a quarantine trailer with a small window
situation: Returning astronauts are whisked into a sealed trailer and greet the cheering crew and a dignitary through glass
visualTropes: sailors spelling a word on deck
jokeHooks: the code ships but must sit in quarantine for 21 days, like a staged rollout
everyone celebrates while the team is still behind glass fixing logs
the dignitary cuts a ribbon on a feature the crew calls beta

title: Rollout on the giant crawler
place: A gravel crawlerway at night under floodlights, a giant tracked transporter carrying an upright rocket at walking pace toward the pad
situation: The crawler creeps toward the pad at one mile an hour while engineers walk alongside and one runs back for something forgotten
cast: crawler driver in a tiny cab
engineer running back to the hangar
jokeHooks: the rollout is slower than walking, like a monorepo build
someone forgot a part and runs back, like a missing file in the release
the crawler stops every few feet for a check, like CI on every commit

title: Survival training after a mock splashdown
place: A tropical jungle shore and swamp, astronaut trainees in silver suits climbing out of a capsule mockup, trainers in a boat
situation: Trainees must survive three days with a survival kit, building shelters from parachutes and fending off curious crabs
visualTropes: a capsule mockup on the sand
a crab stealing a ration bar
jokeHooks: the survival kit has everything except the one tool the docs require
the training mirrors production except the crabs are real
a ration bar labeled lasts forever like a never-expiring token

title: Pad abort with the escape tower
place: A rocket on the pad with a needle-like escape tower on top firing, the capsule yanked skyward away from a fizzling booster
situation: A sensor trips at ignition and the escape tower rips the capsule away, landing it in the ocean while the rocket sits there unharmed
visualTropes: an untouched rocket on the pad
jokeHooks: the abort fires because a flaky sensor reported failure, and everything was fine
a safety net that works perfectly, on a false alarm
the postmortem finds the culprit was a loose plug, like a missing env var
